metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a spike in true outcome, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: if true value > forecast by >10%, reduce next forecast by 5–15%.
- When sentiment history is flat (0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence — apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast mean by 3–7% if sentiment remains unchanged for 10+ days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizons — if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- For 30+ day horizons, model often fails to capture downward trends — if true outcome shows sustained decline >3 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If true outcome includes a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to recognize it — apply “spike decay” rule: if true value drops >10% from peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days.
